summary: EIGHT DAYS AFTER SHE RESIGNED, NOBODY AT ALTR HAS ACKNOWLEDGED IT — AND THE ACCOUNT IS NOW CLOSED. Alex Paige quit on 2026-09-17 at 20:19 ('Hey guys I just want to let you know I’m leaving ALTR...'). Between that message and the close of this window there were exactly six messages in the chat, and not one of them refers to her departure. ALTR's FIRST contact after the resignation came four days and one hour later, on 2026-09-21 at 21:15, and it was an invoice chase: 'Hi love! Just wanted to reach out about closing out your invoice with us ❤️ remaining balance is currently $5,259.90, do you mind shooting that over in the AM?' — followed 6 seconds later by '@alexpaigem' to make sure she saw it. She replied 'No worries' inside two hours, and on 2026-09-23 at 06:27 she posted a receipt photo and 'Final invoice paid'. The last words ALTR ever said to a twelve-month client were Mayson's two-word 'Thanks @alexpaigem'. No 'sorry to hear that'. No reason asked. No exit call. No save attempt. No offboarding, no account handover, no wind-down of DMCA/leak coverage, no confirmation that her balance is now zero. Derrek has still not written in this chat since 2026-08-13 — 43 days — and did not write when she resigned, did not write in the eight days since, and has now permanently lost the chance to. THE ONE THING THAT WENT RIGHT IS MONEY, AND IT WENT ONLY ONE WAY. Stephski put the third figure in twelve months of billing into the chat ($5,259.90) and collected it in 33 hours from a client who had already left — the collection risk this report called HIGH last week evaporated entirely, because the client is more reliable than the agency. Twelve months, not one refused, disputed or withheld payment, and she settled her final balance two days after resigning. WHAT IS STILL OPEN RUNS THE OTHER DIRECTION. The $5,259.90 was a balance, not a statement: no itemised ledger has ever been issued, the $1,989 July 1-14 dispute is 60 days old and was never mentioned in the closeout, the referral/promo money ALTR owes HER is 63 days unresolved and 43 days past Derrek's 'Sending', and the customs sold off Ronnie's 2026-08-25 spreadsheet are 31 days old, unfulfillable, unrefunded and un-mentioned — on an account with a documented $1,560-in-24-hours chargeback history. Nobody at ALTR confirmed the account is settled at zero. SERVICE DECAYED TO NOTHING. Michelle Queue's leak-removal report — the only unbroken cadence this account ever had (eight straight weekly sends through 2026-09-08) — has now missed two consecutive weeks, 17 days since the last send, while DMCA coverage was still nominally live. Ronnie: silent 22 days. Mica: silent since her Sep 17 security advisory. @paigealexxo never posted, 115 days after she first asked. The trial-reels call died at 21 days. Every stale promise on this account has now been closed by churn rather than by delivery. This is the last window with a live chat. The only recoverable value left — an exit conversation, an itemised final ledger both ways, and refunds before chargebacks — is still sitting there untouched, and she is still replying.

Last week the resignation was 12 hours and 46 minutes old and still salvageable. This week it is eight days old, ALTR's first response to it was a bill sent four days later, and the client has paid and gone. The window contained six messages: a payment chase, an @-mention to chase the chase, 'No worries', a receipt, 'Final invoice paid', and 'Thanks @alexpaigem'. That is the complete record of how ALTR handled the departure of a client who paid it for twelve months and never once withheld a cent. Not one person asked why she left. Derrek's silence reached 43 days and was never broken — personal owner contact was the number-one recommendation in five consecutive reports and it is now unactionable. Real credit where it is due: Stephski stated the balance clearly ('remaining balance is currently $5,259.90'), the third figure ever written in this chat, and collected it in 33 hours; the client paid it in full. But that is ALTR protecting its own receivable inside an otherwise total abandonment. Against it: no exit conversation, no reason captured, no save attempt, no offboarding or access handover, no confirmation the account is settled at zero, the $1,989 July dispute 60 days open and never mentioned in the closeout, ALTR's own referral debt to her 63 days unquantified, paid customs 31 days unrefunded on an account with $1,560 of chargeback history, and Michelle Queue's eight-week leak-report streak now two weeks broken. The score is not zero only because she paid, she left warmly, and she is still replying — which means the final ledger and the refunds can still be done today. It will be zero next week if they are not.
